name: formal
comment: Mirrors the Prism `formal` grammar in index.html; keep the two in step.

asm-block.comment: `asm:` and the lines indented deeper than it. Registers, numbers, comments and strings are coloured; the mnemonics and their other operands stay plain instead of being read as variables. The end backreference is the header's indentation: the block closes at the first non-blank line not indented past it.

def-header.comment: `def name(` : the keyword and the function being defined

define.comment: `name: [locality] type` at the start of a line defines a variable; block headers that also end in a colon are keywords and are excluded

patterns.comment: `_` leaves a type or locality to the verifier; `..` in a pattern accepts any array
patterns.name: support.type.placeholder.formal

register.comment: the fourteen registers the dialect names: the CPU registers themselves, so a constant scope rather than a variable one. Themes colour the two families apart (Dark+: blue against light blue; One Dark: orange against red), where `variable.language` is often painted like any other variable.
register.name: constant.language.register.formal

asm-register.comment: inside `asm:` every RISC-V register name, the same list the website's grammar uses
asm-register.name: constant.language.register.formal

variable.comment: any other name: an ordinary variable (`my_variable = 2`). Last, after keywords, types, registers and calls have had their turn.
variable.name: variable.other.formal

builtin-call.comment: `type(x)` and `csr(x)` are assignment forms, not defs
builtin-call.name: support.function.builtin.formal

patterns.comment: two-character comparisons before the single characters, or `!=` splits
patterns.name: keyword.operator.formal
